In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah al-Fath

It is Medinan according to all of them. Some have said that it was revealed between Makkah and Madinah on his return from al-Hudaybiyah; this was related by Miswar ibn Makhramah, Marwan, and others.

Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey, and he said: 'Last night there was revealed to me a surah that is dearer to me than the world and all that is in it,' then he recited: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory﴾." Al-Bukhari related it from al-Qa'nabi, from Malik.

It is also related from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "When we returned from Makkah, after we had been prevented from performing our rites, and we were overcome by a great deal of grief and sorrow, Allah the Exalted revealed this surah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'It is dearer to me than all of the world.'"

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory﴾ means: We have decreed for you a manifest decree. The meaning of "qada'" (decree) here is the judgment of victory over the enemies. In the language, al-fath (victory/opening) is the opening of what was closed; it is said also that it is a joy that removes worry, and from it comes the "opening" of a matter, which is the clarification that leads to the desired goal. As for what the name "al-Fath" was applied to, the majority of scholars and exegetes hold that it refers to the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah. If it is asked: how can a treaty be a victory, when if it is a victory for the Muslims it is also a victory for the disbelievers, since a treaty involves both sides? The answer: this was indeed problematic for Umar, for when Allah the Exalted revealed this surah, Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this a victory?" He said: "Yes."

It is also said that it was the greatest victory in Islam, because when he made peace with the polytheists and they withdrew, he had agreed to suspend hostilities for ten years. The polytheists then mixed with the Muslims, heard the Qur'an, and saw the way of the Messenger of Allah and his Companions, so they came to desire Islam. More people from among the polytheists embraced Islam during the period of the truce than had embraced it during the period of war, and the number of Muslims greatly increased. In this period there embraced Islam: Khalid ibn al-Walid, Amr ibn al-As, Uthman ibn Talhah al-Abdari, and many of the notables of the polytheists. At the expedition of al-Hudaybiyah there was the Pledge of Ridwan, and the promise of the conquest of Khaybar and the victory of the Romans over the Persians. This was among the miracles of the Messenger. This gladdened the Muslims and grieved the polytheists, because the Muslims wished for the victory of the People of the Book, while the polytheists wished for the victory of the Persians and non-Arabs. So Allah fulfilled what the Muslims desired. When the Persians had prevailed over the Romans, the polytheists had said: "Just as the Persians have prevailed over the Romans, so we shall prevail over you." Therefore, when Allah granted the Romans victory over the Persians, that was a sign of the Muslims' victory over the polytheists.

It is also said, regarding al-Hudaybiyah, that it refers to the permission to shave the head and slaughter before the offering reached its place. There is another view regarding the verse: that the intended victory is the conquest of Makkah, because Allah the Exalted had promised him the conquest of Makkah during the expedition of al-Hudaybiyah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 2:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your sins, past and future﴾. Tha'lab said: its meaning is "so that Allah may forgive you," so the lam carries the sense of kay (so that). He said: the real meaning is that He combines forgiveness for you with the conquest, so that His blessing is completed upon you through it. Abu Hatim al-Sijistani, the grammarian, said: the meaning of His saying ﴿That Allah may forgive you﴾ is "Allah will surely forgive you," and when the nun was dropped, the lam took a kasra (lam al-jarr, i.e. the lam was given the vowel of a preposition).

His saying ﴿your sins, past and future﴾ means: what of your sins preceded the time of prophethood, and what came after the time of prophethood. It was also said: what of your sins preceded the conquest, and what came after the conquest. It is related from al-Thawri that he said: "What has been and what will be, as long as you have not done it, and you are going to do it, so it is as if He forgave him before the act."

If someone says: what sin did he have? We say: minor sins; he was protected (ma'sum) from major sins.

In the tafsir of al-Naqqash: he was a worshipper before prophethood according to the law of Ibrahim concerning marriage, divorce, acts of worship, transactions and other matters. He had married Khadijah while she was a polytheist, and likewise he married his daughter Ruqayyah to Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, who was a polytheist, and [likewise] he married his daughter Zaynab to [Abu] al-As ibn al-Rabi', who was a polytheist. These were his sins before prophethood, and Allah the Exalted has forgiven them for him, and that was from him not by way of deliberate intent. It is firmly established from the Prophet ﷺ that he prayed until his feet swelled, and it was said to him: "Do you do this when Allah has forgiven you your sins, past and future?" He said: "Should I not be a grateful servant?"

Al-Damyati mentioned in his tafsir, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the occasion of revelation of the verse is that when Allah the Exalted revealed His saying ﴿And I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾, the polytheists and the Jews rejoiced at it and said: "This is a man who does not know what will be done with him or with his companions, so how can we enter his religion?" Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul al-Ansari said: "Will you enter the religion of a man who does not know what will be done with him?" The Muslims were greatly saddened by that, so Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that Allah may forgive you your sins, past and future﴾, and so on. The Muslims said: "Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah; so what about us?" Then Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾.

His saying ﴿and complete His blessing upon you﴾ means: complete His blessing upon you by granting victory over the enemies, ﴿and He sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers that they might increase in faith along with their faith; and to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth﴾, and by guiding you to the laws of Islam. The conquest mentioned in the verse has been interpreted as guidance to Islam.

His saying ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾ means: He directs you to the straight way.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah will help you with a mighty help﴾, meaning: (a help) with might, not with humiliation in it. There is another view regarding the sense of this verse: that His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest, that Allah may forgive you﴾ has the same meaning as His saying in Surah al-Nasr: ﴿When the help of Allah and the conquest come﴾; so that conquest is this conquest. And His saying: ﴿And you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes, so exalt your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness﴾, so that command to glorify and seek forgiveness is placed here out of order (mudraj). It is as if Allah, exalted is He, said: (﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest﴾, so glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness) ﴿that Allah may forgive you﴾. Abu al-Husayn Ibn Faris mentioned this in his tafsir, and he made this command an answer to a question from one who asks about the verse: how can His saying ﴿that He may forgive﴾ be made an answer to His saying ﴿Indeed, We have given you﴾, when both are from Allah, exalted is He? So he answered him in this way.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 4:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sent down tranquility (al-sakinah) into the hearts of the believers﴾. We have already explained that al-sakinah is derived from al-sukun (stillness, calm), and its reality is stillness (al-sukun) toward Allah's promise and trust in Him. It is also said: al-sakinah is what Allah Most High inspired into the believers of patience and reliance upon Him in all matters.

His saying: ﴿in the hearts of the believers, that they might increase in faith along with their faith﴾, meaning: confirmation (tasdiq) added to their confirmation. It is also said: certainty (yaqin) added to their certainty. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that Allah Most High commanded the believers to bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. When they accepted that, He added to them the five daily prayers; when they accepted that, He added to them zakat; then He added to them the hajj; then He added to them jihad. When He had perfected its legislation, He revealed His saying: ﴿This day I have perfected for you your religion﴾.

His saying: ﴿And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the hosts of the heavens and the earth. Were He to empower the least of His creation over the entire world, it would subdue them. It is also said: "to Him belong the armies of the heavens and the earth" means: what Allah created in the heavens of the angels, and what Allah created in the earth of the jinn, mankind and others.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: Knowing of His creation, Wise in His governance.

The Most High said: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and remove from them their misdeeds; and that is in the sight of Allah a great triumph﴾. That is: a great salvation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 6:

His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women, who assume about Allah an assumption of evil.﴾ The meaning of "an assumption of evil" here is that they had supposed that the affair of Muhammad would not be completed and would soon come to nothing. It is said: when the Messenger set out for Makkah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah with his companions, intending to perform the minor pilgrimage (ʿumrah), and carried with him nothing of weapons except swords in their sheaths, the hypocrites and the rest of the disbelievers said: Muhammad will never turn back from this course of his, and he and his companions will perish. This is the meaning of "an assumption of evil."

His statement: ﴿The evil turn of fortune is upon them.﴾ It has been recited as "dāʾirat as-sawʾ" with the sīn pronounced with a ḍammah (rafʿ), and the two meanings are close, i.e., upon them is the consequence of destruction. It is also said that its meaning is: for them is the evil outcome, not for the Messenger.

His statement: ﴿And Allah has become angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and it is an evil destination.﴾ That is: wretched is the place of return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 7:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth﴾. In the exegesis (tafsir) it is said that the hypocrites said: "What will Muhammad's companions avail him? If he prevails over his own people, how will he prevail over all the Arabs, and Kisra and Caesar? Muhammad has only promised his companions delusion." So Allah the Exalted sent down His saying: ﴿And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth﴾. Its meaning: victory comes from Me, and all the soldiers are Mine. Whomever I wish to help, that is not difficult for Me, whether his enemies are few or many.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾: Mighty (mani') in granting victory, Wise (hakim) in His management.

And the Most High's saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness﴾, meaning: a witness over your community on the Day of Resurrection. It is also said: a witness to the conveying of the command and the prohibition.

And His saying: ﴿and a bringer of good tidings﴾, meaning: a bringer of good tidings to those who obey.

And His saying: ﴿and a warner﴾, meaning: one who warns those who disobey.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 9:

And His saying: ﴿that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: so that you, O people, may believe in Allah and His Messenger.

And His saying: ﴿and honour him﴾, meaning: glorify him (ta'zim). It was recited in the irregular reading (shadh): "wa-tu'azzizuhu" (and strengthen him), meaning: you advance with what becomes a source of might for him.

And His saying: ﴿and revere him﴾, meaning: magnify him and exalt him. It is also said: "wa-tu'adhdhiruhu" (and support him), meaning: [support him] with the sword, and this is the well-known opinion. If someone asks: to whom does the pronoun (al-ha') refer? The answer is in two respects. The first: it refers to the Messenger. The second: it refers to Allah, exalted is He.

And His saying: ﴿and glorify Him morning and evening﴾ is directed to Allah without any disagreement.

The glorification (tasbih) at dawn (bukrah) is the Morning Prayer (salat al-subh), and at evening (asil) it is the Noon and Afternoon Prayers (salat al-zuhr and al-'asr).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you﴾ refers to the pledge on the Day of al-Hudaybiyah. They had pledged to him that they would not flee, and in another narration: they pledged to him unto death.

His saying: ﴿They are only pledging allegiance to Allah﴾ means: whoever takes the covenant from you has taken the covenant from me, and whoever pledges allegiance to you has pledged allegiance to me. It is also reported from some of them: whoever enters Islam has pledged allegiance to Allah, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their property...﴾ the verse.

His saying: ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands﴾ means: the hand of Allah in aid and favour upon them is over their hands, through their obedience to you. It is also said its meaning is: the hand of Allah in fulfilling His promise ﴿is over their hands﴾ in fulfilling their covenant. It is also said: Allah's beneficence toward them is greater than their beneficence toward you through support, and Allah's favour upon them is greater than their favour upon you in accepting what you have brought.

His saying: ﴿So whoever breaks [his oath]﴾ means: whoever breaks the covenant.

His saying: ﴿Then he breaks it only to the detriment of himself﴾ means: the burden of breaking his covenant falls upon him. It is said: the verse was revealed concerning al-Jadd ibn Qays, who was among the hypocrites. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the pledge with his companions, the Pledge of Ridwan, he hid under the belly of a camel and did not pledge allegiance. The meaning of breaking (nakth) is abandonment.

His saying: ﴿And whoever fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah, He will give him a great reward﴾ means: abundant.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 11:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The ones who lagged behind among the Bedouins will say to you﴾. The verse was revealed concerning Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ashja' and Aslam, who had stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the Battle of al-Hudaybiyah, and they offered as an excuse being preoccupied with their wealth and families. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned, they came making excuses, and Allah, Exalted is He, revealed this verse concerning them.

His saying: ﴿Our wealth and our families have kept us busy, so ask forgiveness for us﴾, i.e., seek forgiveness from Allah, Exalted is He, on our behalf.

His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾, meaning: they do not care whether you ask forgiveness for them or leave off asking forgiveness for them, because of their hypocrisy; they only display the request for forgiveness out of taqiyyah (dissimulation) and fear. This applies to the hypocrites among these tribes, not to all of them, for among them there were Muslims whose Islam was sound.

His saying: ﴿Say: "Who then has any power for you against Allah, if He intends harm for you or intends benefit for you?"﴾, i.e., who will ward off the punishment of Allah from you, and who will prevent you from Allah if He wills to punish you?

His saying: ﴿if He intends harm for you or intends benefit for you﴾, i.e., the matter in all of this is in His hand alone. His saying: ﴿Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾, i.e., Knowing.

It is said regarding His saying ﴿Our wealth has kept us busy﴾, i.e., there is no one to tend to it for us.

His saying: ﴿and our families﴾, i.e., there is no one to take our place in attending to their affairs.

His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: in their hearts was doubt.

His saying: ﴿Say: "Who then has any power for you against Allah if He intends harm for you"﴾, i.e., defeat.

His saying: ﴿or intends benefit for you﴾, i.e., victory and booty.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, ever.﴾ We have already explained their thought. ﴿And that was made attractive in your hearts﴾, meaning: Satan made it attractive.

And His saying: ﴿And you thought an evil thought﴾. We have already explained its meaning.

And His saying: ﴿And you were a people ruined (bura)﴾, meaning: lost. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is the one in whom there is no good. It is said that in the dialect of the Azd of Oman, "bur" means corrupt. It is also said: a man is "bur," two men are "buran," and men are "bur." It is said: "Their deeds became ruined (bura) and their dwellings became graves." It was also said: "bura" means those whose hearts are corrupt, neither doers of good nor pious. In the tafsir it is related that their thought was that Muhammad and his companions would be killed on that course and would never return to Madinah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 13:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger, then indeed We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The saʿir (blaze) is the sixth level of Hell."

The Most High's saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ Its apparent meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The ones who stayed behind will say, when you set out to take spoils: "Let us follow you."﴾ The occasion of revelation of the verse: Allah, exalted is He, had promised the people of al-Hudaybiyya the spoils of Khaybar. These Bedouins who had stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah and had entertained an evil assumption desired the spoils of Khaybar, and Allah had made the spoils of Khaybar exclusively for the people of al-Hudaybiyya. When the Prophet and his Companions returned to Medina and set out before Khaybar, these Bedouins came, asked the Messenger of Allah for permission to be with him on this expedition, and said: "Let us follow you."

And His saying: ﴿They want to change the word of Allah.﴾ That is: the ruling of Allah which He decreed regarding the spoils of Khaybar, that they were exclusively for the people of (Medina), since they coveted a share of them. It is also said that the meaning of His saying: ﴿They want to change the word of Allah﴾ is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "You will never follow us; thus has Allah said beforehand."﴾ So they wanted to change this word which Allah had spoken, and to show that we went out and fought, contrary to what Allah had said. In the exegesis: when they said, "Let us follow you," the Companions of the Messenger of Allah said to them: "We permit you to fight on the condition that you are volunteers in the fighting, with no share for you in the booty, because the booty of Khaybar is exclusively for the people of al-Hudaybiyya."

And His saying: ﴿Say: "You will never follow us; thus has Allah said beforehand."﴾ According to the first opinion, "You will never follow us" is absolute, and according to the second opinion, "Say: You will never follow us" is for the purpose of taking the booty.

And His saying: ﴿Thus has Allah said beforehand﴾ means: the ruling of Allah from before.

And His saying: ﴿Then they will say, "No, you envy us."﴾ That is: you did not permit us to follow you, out of envy of you toward us, lest we obtain what you obtain.

And His saying: ﴿Rather, they understood little.﴾ That is: they did not know what was for them and against them in the religion, except a little.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 16:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Say to the desert Arabs who stayed behind: You will be called to a people of great might; you will fight them, or they will submit.﴾ The most sound of the opinions is that they are the Banu Hanifa, who showed great might when they fought the Muslims alongside Musaylima the Liar. Rafi' ibn Khadij said: "We did not know the meaning of His words, ﴿of great might﴾, until ﴿You will be called to a people of great might; you will fight them, or they will submit. So if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward﴾. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, called us to fight Musaylima, and that war was a severe war for the Muslims, in which many of the Companions were martyred."

It is said: seven hundred men from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah were martyred in it, among them Zayd ibn al-Khattab, the brother of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and 'Ukasha ibn [Muhsin].

The second opinion: His words ﴿of great might﴾ refer to Hawazin and Thaqif. This was said by al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas.

The third opinion: they are Persia, and the war with them was the most severe war against the Muslims in the time of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him.

In the first opinion, and in this opinion, there is evidence for the caliphate of Abu Bakr and Umar, because they called the Muslims to fight Musaylima and to fight Persia. The Battle of al-Qadisiyya occurred with Persia, in which Rustam, commander of the non-Arab army, was killed; also the Battle of Jalula and the Battle of Nahavand, which is called "the Conquest of Conquests." After it, no standing power remained for them, their kingdom was torn apart, and Allah confirmed the Prophet's supplication when he said: "O Allah, tear apart the kingdom of Persia." It is also narrated that when Khosrow tore up the letter of the Prophet, and this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "May Allah tear apart his kingdom." And from Ka'b al-Ahbar, he said concerning His words ﴿to a people of great might﴾: "They are the Romans, and with them is the Great Battle at the end of time."

The most sound of the opinions is the first opinion, because Allah, may He be exalted, says ﴿you will fight them, or they will submit﴾, and its meaning is "or they will submit (aslamu)." This applies only to apostates, from whom the jizya may not be taken; as for Magians and Christians, the jizya may be taken from them. As for Mujahid, he applied the verse to the people of idols.

His words ﴿So if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward﴾ mean: Paradise.

His words ﴿But if you turn away, as you turned away before﴾ mean: if you turn away as you turned away before.

His words ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ mean: a painful (wajī'an) punishment. If it is said: He mentioned in this verse His words ﴿You will be called to a people of great might﴾, and He said in another verse ﴿Say: You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me﴾, and they fought only with Abu Bakr and Umar, and did not fight with the Messenger...

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾. It means: there is no blame upon those who stayed behind from you, because of these excuses, from the expedition of al-Hudaybiyah.

Al-haraj (blame) means sin. The meaning of the verse is that God, may He be exalted, permitted the spoils of Khaybar to the people who stayed behind from the expedition of al-Hudaybiyah because of these excuses. It has been said that these people were: Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh, his mother Amina bint Abd al-Muttalib, Abd Allah ibn Umm Maktum the blind, and others.

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever obeys God and His Messenger, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow; and whoever turns away, He will punish him with a painful punishment﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 18:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree﴾. The well-known account concerning this verse is that when the Prophet set out for Makkah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, performing ʿumrah, he and his Companions took the sacrificial animals (al-hady) along with themselves. When they reached al-Hudaybiyah, which is a well at a known place on the edge of the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), the area was named after the well. A miracle of the Messenger of Allah also appeared at this well: "The Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah be pleased with them, when they arrived there, drained it until no water remained, so they complained to the Messenger of Allah of their thirst. The Messenger of Allah came and sat on the edge of the well and asked for water, rinsed his mouth with it and poured it into the well. The well then overflowed with water, the people drew water, they watered the riding animals, and it never ran dry afterwards."

Returning to the origin of the story: "When they reached al-Hudaybiyah, the camel of the Prophet, al-Qaswa, knelt down. They urged her to rise but she did not rise. They said: 'al-Qaswa has become stubborn.' The Messenger of Allah said: 'She has not become stubborn, nor is that her habit, but she was held back by the One who held back the Elephant. By Allah, they will not ask me for any arrangement in which the honouring of the sanctity of Allah's Sanctuary is involved, except that I will grant it to them.' Then he summoned ʿUmar and wished to send him to the people of Makkah to seek their permission to enter, so that he might perform his ʿumrah and slaughter his sacrificial animal. ʿUmar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have no kin or clan there, and they know how intense my enmity toward them is, and I fear for myself at their hands. But I will direct you to someone who is dearer to them than I am, ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan.' He said: 'And who is that?' He said: 'ʿUthman.' So he sent him to Makkah. Then word reached the Prophet that ʿUthman had been killed. It is also related from some of them that Iblis went out and said: 'ʿUthman has been killed.' Thereupon the Prophet stood up, leaned against the tree, which was a samurah tree, and gave the pledge along with his Companions. This is the Pledge of Ridwan (Bayʿat al-Ridwan). He had pledged them to fight until death, and it is said he pledged them not to flee."

Opinions differ regarding the number of people. Ibn Abi Awfa said: "One thousand three hundred." Jabir said: "One thousand four hundred," and this is the more correct view. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas: "One thousand five hundred." Then it became clear that ʿUthman had not been killed.

There is another opinion regarding the verse, narrated by Ibn Abi Za'idah from al-Sha'bi, who said: "The pledge mentioned in the verse by Allah is the pledge of the Messenger of Allah with the seventy men of the Ansar on the night of al-ʿAqabah. The account concerning it is that seventy men from the people of Madinah came to meet the Prophet during the days of Hajj before the Hijrah, led by Abu Umamah As'ad ibn Zurarah. The Prophet went out, accompanied by al-ʿAbbas, at night until they reached al-ʿAqabah, and these seventy from the people of Madinah were present. Al-ʿAbbas said to them: 'Let your speaker speak and not prolong it, for there are spies upon you, and if Quraysh recognise your position they will harm you.' As'ad ibn Zurarah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, stipulate for your Lord and stipulate for yourself, and mention what we will have if we accept.' The Prophet said: 'I stipulate for my Lord that you associate nothing with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect your own selves and your children from.' He said: 'What will we have if we do that?' He said: 'Paradise.' He said: 'We are pleased.'"

It is narrated that Iblis cried out at al-ʿAqabah: "O assembly of Quraysh, these youths have gathered with Muhammad to pledge allegiance against you." When they heard that, the Prophet and those men dispersed, and the polytheists came but found no one. The sound opinion is the first view.

As for His words: ﴿So He knew what was in their hearts﴾, that is, of truthfulness and loyalty. It is said: it means sincerity.

As for His words: ﴿So He sent down tranquility upon them﴾, that is, serenity (al-tuma'ninah). It is said: trust in Allah's promise, patience upon Allah's command. It is said: certainty of loyalty.

As for His words: ﴿And rewarded them with an imminent victory﴾, that is, the conquest of Khaybar. It is said: the conquest of Makkah. The first is the well-known view.

Almighty God's words: ﴿And many spoils that they will take﴾ — meaning the wealth of Khaybar. They had much wealth in properties, date palms, and other things.

And His words: ﴿And Allah has always been Mighty and Wise﴾ — we have already explained this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah has promised you much booty that you will take﴾. Mujahid said: its meaning is the spoils taken from the disbelievers until the Hour arises. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the spoils of Persia and Rome. It was also said: the conquest of Mecca.

His saying: ﴿So He has hastened for you this﴾, that is, the spoils of Khaybar.

His saying: ﴿and has restrained the hands of the people from you﴾. In the tafsir it is related that the Banu Asad and Ghatafan were allies of the Jews of Khaybar. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for Khaybar, Asad and Ghatafan intended to raid Medina, but Allah cast terror into their hearts and they dispersed. It is also narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) first turned towards them intending to fight alongside them, but they fled and dispersed and left the people of Khaybar, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to Khaybar and conquered it. It is said: "restrained the hands of the people from you" means all the polytheists. Among the nations there was none more humiliated and few in number than the Arabs, so Allah honoured them through Islam, enriched them with the treasures of the non-Arabs and the Romans, and made them inheritors of their lands, their homes and their wealth. The first time humiliation entered the non-Arabs was the Battle of Dhi Qar, which is a place where Kisra sent his armies to the Banu Shayban to fight alongside them, on account of a long story. They fought at Dhi Qar, and the Arabs made their password the name of Muhammad. Their leader said to them: "Make your password the name of this Qurashi who has gone out calling people to Allah, the Exalted." They fought, Allah routed the polytheists, and most of Kisra's soldiers were killed. When this reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "Today the Arabs have been given justice against the non-Arabs, and by me they were helped." From that time humiliation entered the non-Arabs and their kingdom perished.

His saying: ﴿and that it may be a sign for the believers﴾, that is, a miracle. The sign lies in the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) promise of the conquest of Khaybar and the spoils of the non-Arabs and the Romans, and this was fulfilled soon after.

His saying: ﴿and guides you to a straight path﴾, that is, leads you to the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted.

Allah's saying: ﴿And others you were not able to conquer, but Allah has encompassed them﴾. That is, the lands of the non-Arabs (al-'ajam). It is also said: the land of Makkah. It is also said: all the lands that Allah has opened, and will open them until the Hour comes.

His saying: ﴿Allah has encompassed them﴾. That is, His knowledge has encompassed them.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾. That is, Capable.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if those who disbelieve fought you, they would surely turn their backs in flight.﴾ That is: they would be routed, and victory would belong to them.

And His saying: ﴿Then they would find no protector or helper.﴾ We have explained this before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The way of Allah which has already taken place before﴾. That is: Allah established this sunnah (way/practice), which is the granting of victory to His allies and the destruction of His enemies. It is also said: it is that the final outcome belongs to the believers. The meaning is: this sunnah which I have established for you is My sunnah concerning those who passed away before you.

And His saying: ﴿And you will not find any change in the way of Allah﴾. That is: any alteration.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 24:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah﴾. Abdullah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani narrated that the Prophet was sitting under the tree, taking the pledge (bay'ah) from his companions. And in another narration: "With him were Ali ibn Abi Talib and Suhayl ibn Amr, who were writing the document of the truce (sulh). Thirty young men of the polytheists, who had come from Makkah with the intention of [harming] the Messenger of Allah, then rose up against us."

The Messenger of Allah invoked [Allah], and Allah took away their sight, so we stood up, brought them, and led them by the reins to the Messenger of Allah. He said: "Do you have a covenant? Do you have a pledge of safety?" They said: "No." So he released them, and Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them﴾.

Hammad ibn Salamah narrated from Thabit, from Anas, who said: Eighty men armed with weapons descended from the mountain of al-Tan'im, and the companions of the Messenger of Allah seized them and brought them to the Prophet, who spared them and released them, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

His saying: ﴿in the valley of Makkah﴾ means: al-Hudaybiyah, and he called it the valley of Makkah only because of its nearness to Makkah.

His saying: ﴿after He had given you victory over them﴾ has already been explained.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾ means: Knowing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 25:

God's words: ﴿They are those who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and the offering detained from reaching its place of sacrifice.﴾ That is: and they barred the offering detained. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), and its meaning is: held back.

His words: ﴿that it reach its place of sacrifice﴾ That is: its place of slaughter (manḥar). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had driven seventy camels.

His words: ﴿And were it not for believing men and believing women﴾ The people of exegesis (ahl al-tafsīr) said: the meaning of the verse is that men and women had embraced Islam in Mecca and remained there, mixed with the polytheists, and their whereabouts were not known. So God, exalted is He, said: were it not for them, meaning the people we have mentioned, ﴿you did not know that you might trample them﴾, meaning: you might strike them and harm them unknowingly, if you entered as warriors and fighters.

His words: ﴿so that a sin would befall you on their account without knowledge﴾ That is: a reproach (sabba), and it is said: a blemish and blame. Its meaning is that the disbelievers would blame you, saying: they kill the people of their own religion. It is also said regarding the ma'arra (sin/liability): it is the obligation of blood-money (diyya) upon killing.

His words: ﴿that God might admit into His mercy whom He wills﴾ There is an omitted supposition in it, and its meaning is: He prevented [fighting] between you and them, so that God might admit into His mercy whom He wills, that is, into Islam, whom He wills.

His words: ﴿Had they been separated﴾ That is: had they been distinguished, that is, had the Muslims separated from the disbelievers, ﴿We would have punished those of them who disbelieved with a painful punishment﴾. Its meaning is: had it not been that the sin would befall you and the Muslims were mixed with the disbelievers, We would have punished those who disbelieved, that is, by the sword, through killing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When those who disbelieved had placed in their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah)﴾. Al-hamiyyah (zealotry) is arrogance and refusal to accept something out of anger. Arrogance is of two kinds: praiseworthy and blameworthy. It is said: "So-and-so is a protector of his sanctuary (hamma hawmatahu)," meaning he defends his protected territory. The meaning of "the zealotry of the time of ignorance" here is that the disbelievers refused to let the Prophet and his Companions enter Makkah that year. They said: "Muhammad will never enter upon us against our will as long as one of us remains." That was arrogance and zealotry on their part. Then, when the Messenger made the treaty with them, it was stipulated in the treaty that he would return this year, and come back the following year in that same month, perform his rites (nusk), stay three days, and then depart.

There is another opinion regarding the verse: that the meaning of "the zealotry of the time of ignorance" is that Suhayl ibn 'Amr, together with Huwaytib ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza, came to conclude [the treaty]. ﴿...the zealotry of the time of ignorance. So Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and made them adhere to the word﴾ of the treaty agreement. When it was time for the writing (al-kitbah), the Prophet said to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Suhayl said: "We do not know what 'the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate' is! Write as we write: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" The Muslims said: "There is no god but Allah," in amazement at their words, and the mountains of Tihamah echoed with it. Then he said: "Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon." Suhayl said: "If we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have fought you. Write: This is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah has agreed upon." 'Ali wrote that. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am Muhammad the Messenger of Allah, and I am Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah."

Also among the terms of the treaty: whoever came to the Prophet from the polytheists as a Muslim during the period of the truce would be returned to them, and whoever went from the Muslims to the disbelievers as an apostate would not be returned to them. All of this was from the zealotry of the time of ignorance. At these conditions, a trial befell 'Umar, and he came to the Messenger of Allah and said: "Are you not the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Are we not upon the truth?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Why should we give the inferior terms regarding our religion?" meaning: why should we accept the lesser option for ourselves? The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am the Messenger of Allah, and He will not neglect me." He then went to Abu Bakr and mentioned to him the same thing, and he said to him: "He is the Messenger of Allah, and He will never neglect him. Hold fast to the stirrup (al-gharz)." Then Suhayl ibn 'Amr embraced Islam after that, his Islam was good, and he stood in Islam in notable positions.

His saying: ﴿So Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾ — we have already explained the meaning of tranquillity (sakinah), and the meaning here is: steadfastness in the religion alongside these matters.

His saying: ﴿and made them adhere to the word of piety (kalimat al-taqwa)﴾ — Ibn al-Tufayl narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet, that it is: "There is no god but Allah."

In the well-known report from 'Umar, he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah say: 'I know a word which, when a servant says it sincerely from his soul, enters Paradise, and I do not know what it is.' Then he said: 'I know what it is: the word which his uncle was pressed upon (alussa 'alayha 'ammuhu), meaning he insisted that his uncle say it, and it is: There is no god but Allah.'" And from al-Zuhri: the word of piety is "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."

His saying: ﴿and they were more worthy of it and its people﴾ — meaning they were fit for this word and worthy of it. It is also said: they were its people in the knowledge and judgment of Allah, and this is the more correct view.

His saying: ﴿and Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾ — meaning: Knowing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 48, verse 27:

The words of God Most High: ﴿Indeed Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision with truth﴾. The exegetes said: The Prophet saw in his dream that he entered Makkah with his companions, some having shaved their heads and some having shortened their hair. He related this to his companions, and they had no doubt that it was true, and they thought it would happen in that same year. The Prophet and his companions performed 'umrah and set out on that basis. When the polytheists prevented them from the House and they turned back, the Muslims were overcome with severe grief and thought they would not enter. Then Allah revealed this verse. The meaning of His words ﴿Indeed Allah fulfilled﴾ is: Allah made His Messenger's vision come true, i.e., the vision, in truth.

His words ﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security, with your heads shaved and [your hair] shortened, not fearing﴾: this fulfilment took place in the second year, when they performed the 'umrat al-qada' (the make-up 'umrah).

His words ﴿And He knew what you did not know﴾ mean: the time of the vision's realization.

His words ﴿So He made, besides that, a near victory﴾ mean: the conquest of Khaybar. There is a question concerning the verse ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, and sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾, which is well known, and concerning His words ﴿if Allah wills﴾: what is the meaning of ﴿if Allah wills﴾, when Allah Most High is the One who gives the information, and what He informs of is certain to occur, and the exception (al-istithna') only applies to something that may or may not be? The answer has several aspects. The first: the meaning of ﴿if Allah wills﴾ is "when Allah wills."

The second aspect: the verse is in inverted order (al-taqdim wa al-ta'khir), and its meaning is: You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque in security, with your heads shaved and [your hair] shortened, not fearing, if Allah wills.

The third aspect: there were people with the Prophet at the revelation of this verse, some of whom were absent and some of whom died before the promised event came to pass. So the exception applies to this: that some of them, or all of them, will enter.

The fourth aspect, which is the most preferable: Allah Most High said ﴿if Allah wills﴾ here according to what He loves, approves of, and commands His servants. He commanded them to make an exception (to say "if Allah wills") regarding what they report of future matters, and to promise them with it, as Allah Most High said: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed I will do that tomorrow," except [with the condition], "if Allah wills"﴾. This is a command to Him and to the whole Ummah. So He said ﴿if Allah wills﴾, even though He knows that the act will occur, so that the believers may follow this example and not abandon this phrase regarding what they report of matters whose occurrence they do not know. Al-Azhari said: It is as if He said: Since you said "if Allah wills" regarding what you knew would occur, then it is more fitting that you say "if Allah wills" regarding what you do not know will occur.

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾. That is, over all religions. It is well known that Jesus, peace be upon him, will descend from the sky, break the cross, kill the swine, and no Jew or Christian will remain except that he embraces Islam. At that time the war will lay down its burdens, and wealth will overflow until no one accepts it.

His statement: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾. That is, as a witness.

((٢٨} ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval. Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. That is their likeness in

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 48, verse 29:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God﴾. This verse is a testimony from God, the Exalted, to His Messenger that he is in truth, and that he is truly His Messenger.

His saying: ﴿And those with him﴾, meaning: his Companions.

His saying: ﴿Harsh against the disbelievers﴾, i.e., severe and strong against them. This is in the sense of His saying: (﴿mighty against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾), i.e., they are mutually affectionate and connected among themselves. It is also in the sense of His saying: ﴿humble toward the believers﴾.

His saying: ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating﴾, i.e., bowing and prostrating.

His saying: ﴿seeking bounty from God and approval﴾, i.e., Paradise and the promised reward.

His saying: ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the effect of prostration﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it refers to the Day of Resurrection, and that is from the traces of ablution, as he (ﷺ) said: "My community will come with bright marks from the traces of ablution." On this view, (the believers) will have bright faces from the effect of ablution and prayer. ʿIkrimah said: "from the effect of prostration" is the dust on the foreheads, for they used to prostrate on the earth. Al-Hasan said: it is the good bearing. It is reported from Saʿid ibn Jubayr: it is humility and lowliness, and this is also a narration from Ibn ʿAbbas. It is said: it is the paleness of the face from staying up at night, and this is a well-known opinion.

His saying: ﴿That is their likeness in the Torah﴾, i.e., their description in the Torah.

His saying: ﴿And their likeness in the Gospel﴾. Some said: the pause is on His saying: ﴿That is their likeness in the Torah﴾, and His saying: ﴿And their likeness in the Gospel﴾ is a new sentence, meaning: their description in the Gospel is like a seed-crop. Others said: the pause is on His saying: ﴿in the Gospel﴾.

His saying: ﴿like a seed-crop﴾, its meaning: they are like a seed-crop.

His saying: ﴿It sends out its shoot﴾, i.e., its offshoots. It is said: "the crop shot out" (ashta'a al-zar') when it put forth offshoots. The meaning of offshoots is that from a single grain there sprout ten ears, or fewer or more.

His saying: ﴿then strengthens it﴾, i.e., it strengthened it. It is read: "fa-azarahu" without the long vowel, and it has the same meaning as the first.

His saying: ﴿then it becomes thick﴾, i.e., it became firm, grew strong and was powerful.

His saying: ﴿and stands firm on its stalk﴾, i.e., it stood erect on its stem.

His saying: ﴿pleasing the sowers﴾, i.e., the cultivators. All of this is a parable of the Prophet and his Companions, and a mention of their description and of how God strengthened the Prophet through them and gave him victory by them.

It is reported from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq that he said: ﴿And those with him﴾ is Abu Bakr; ﴿harsh against the disbelievers﴾ is ʿUmar; ﴿merciful among themselves﴾ is ʿUthman; ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating﴾ is ʿAli, may God be pleased with them; ﴿seeking bounty from God and approval﴾ is the Ten.

And His saying: ﴿like a seed-crop﴾ is Muhammad; ﴿It sends out its shoot﴾ is Abu Bakr; ﴿then strengthens it﴾ is with ʿUmar; ﴿then it becomes thick﴾ is with ʿUthman; ﴿and stands firm on its stalk﴾ is with ʿAli, may God be pleased with them all. This is a strange opinion, mentioned by al-Naqqash. The chosen and well-known view is the first opinion: that the verse refers to all the Companions of the Prophet without specification, and this is the view of the exegetes.

His saying: ﴿That He may enrage the disbelievers by them﴾, i.e., that rage may enter their hearts.

His saying: ﴿God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward﴾. They differed concerning His saying: ﴿among them﴾. Some said: "min" here is for specifying the kind, not for partitive meaning. Al-Zajjaj said: it is for isolating the category, and the intended meaning is not some of them, since all of them are believers and for them is forgiveness and a great reward.

It is reported from Ibn ʿUrwa who said: "We were with Malik ibn Anas, and they mentioned a man who hated the Companions of the Messenger of God. Malik said: whoever wakes up with rage in his heart against the Companions of the Messenger of God, this verse has struck him: ﴿That He may enrage the disbelievers by them﴾."

The second opinion: the meaning of His saying: ﴿among them﴾ is: whoever of them remains firm in faith and righteous deeds, for him is forgiveness and a great reward. This was cited by al-Nahhas in his tafsir.
